en: Lagundi is a scientifically proven Philippine medicinal plant approved by the DOH for relieving coughs and asthma.
The PHIVOLCS earthquake drill teaches Filipinos the Duck, Cover, and Hold technique to protect the head from falling debris.
Filipino scientist Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to keep premature babies warm in rural areas without electricity.
The Department of Health promotes the proper seven-step handwashing technique using soap and water to prevent diarrheal diseases.
The Pinggang Pinoy food plate guide helps children balance rice, vegetables, and protein for healthy daily meals.
Boiling drinking water for at least three minutes kills harmful bacteria and prevents cholera in Philippine communities.
Performing weekly search-and-destroy strategies like covering water containers prevents mosquitoes from breeding and spreading dengue fever in neighborhoods.
Wearing a wide-brimmed hat and applying sunscreen protects Filipino children from harmful ultraviolet rays during outdoor flag ceremonies.
The Bureau of Fire Protection teaches the Stop, Drop, and Roll method to safely extinguish clothes if they catch fire.
PHIVOLCS issues color-coded alert levels to warn communities about volcanic eruptions, helping them evacuate before dangerous ashfall occurs.
The Department of Health distributes free toothbrushes and teaches proper brushing to prevent dental caries among public school students.
Keeping raw meat separate from fresh vegetables in the refrigerator prevents cross-contamination and food poisoning during family fiesta preparations.
